answer: MuSig2 lets several Schnorr signers combine their public keys into one aggregate key, then produce a single joint signature that verifies against that aggregate. Each participant contributes a partial signature computed from its own secret plus a nonce commitment, and the parts are summed, so the result looks like one ordinary Schnorr signature. An atlas of fake identities cannot help a farm here, because a lotus of new keys still needs each secret to sign, and the beacon of verification only lights when every partial signature is genuine.
